q1: SELECT EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(EMAIL) >1
q2: SELECT EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ID) >1
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(EMAIL) >1
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ID) >1
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent. Q1 checks for duplicate emails by counting the occurrences of each email in the PERSON table and selecting those with more than one occurrence. Q2, on the other hand, groups by the first column (EMAIL) and checks if there are more than one distinct IDs for each email.
counterexample_dsp: A test database with at least two people having the same email address, but different IDs.
q1_validation_sql: SELECT EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(EMAIL) >1
q2_validation_sql: SELECT EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ID) >1
